quotes.quote: the lanterns are a mirror, and each watcher sees in them the lamp of his own house

differs: The Lanterns of Nowhere, a pamphlet of 1956, already calls the lanterns a mirror of each watcher's own lamp; Bo Fixture tells the idea as his own and places it in the late 1950s.

images.caption: The title page of The Lanterns of Nowhere, a fictional pamphlet of 1956.
Ivo Fixture, the fictional author of the pamphlet, on the pilot steps.

document.title: The Nowhere Letters
document.provenance: An unsigned typescript left at the Nowhere Gazette in 1990; nobody has said who wrote it, and the harbour board holds no copy.

passages.text: The lantern was towed out on a barge every night of that week, and the crew was told to keep its lamps dark.

quotes.quote: The lantern was towed out on a barge every night of that week

differs: The Nowhere Letters say the lantern was towed out on a barge each night; the tellers say it hung in the air.
